purpose: Independent behavioral confirmation of the complete V2-M1 through V2-M3 authorization chain on fresh data

amendment_record.reason: OnlineEntityGraph._probabilistic_assign's beam-search association cost had no term discouraging a track from claiming a detection that some OTHER active track's own predicted position fits better. The V2-I1 system-integration probe (docs/experiments/V2_I1_INTEGRATION_REPORT.md, friction 6) traced a concrete failure of this on development seed 30001: the self track (index 3, exact-position-matched almost every step) was silently mis-associated to a different physical entity around step 31 during a close encounter with a distractor seeded to cross its path, corrupting that track's theta/autonomous_velocity on the very same update and permanently severing it from the true self position - an identity switch, not a signal-strength problem, and not fixable from the integration layer since the corrupted association happens inside this locked component's own beam search. This amendment adds an `identity_switch_penalty_weight` constructor parameter (default 0.0, a hard no-op: `_identity_switch_penalty` short-circuits and returns exactly 0.0 before doing any work, so every existing caller's cost values are unchanged bit-for-bit, not just numerically close). When enabled, each candidate (track, detection) pairing's cost gets an added penalty proportional to how much closer some OTHER active track's own prediction is to that detection than this track's is - discouraging the pairing that would poach a detection more rightfully belonging to a rival, which is the concrete precondition for a switch. Verified empirically, not just argued: development-split results for V2-M2 (all three association modes: results/V2-M2-probabilistic-development-summary.json, results/V2-M2-hard-map-development-summary.json, results/V2-M2-nearest-development-summary.json, plus the legacy results/V2-M2-summary.json) and V2-M3 (results/V2-M3-body-graph-development-summary.json and its no-causal-likelihood ablation) were captured before this change and re-run after it with the new code's default parameter; every field is byte-for-byte identical except cpu_wall_seconds (a timing measurement, not a behavioral output). No existing caller (v2_m2.py, v2_m3_hypotheses.py, v2_m1_m3_confirmation.py) passes the new parameter, so none of their behavior changes. The already-published v2 confirmation result and its reported metrics remain the authoritative one-shot evidence for the historical M1-M3 chain; this amendment does not authorize or require a new confirmation run.

scope_statement.claim: Fresh-data behavioral confirmation of control discovery, probabilistic identity retention, and calibrated complete-body graph selection
not_claimed: Direct serialization or state handoff from the historical M1 implementation into M2
More than two complete body hypotheses
scope_statement.composition_fact: M2 relearns control relations and M3 extends the M2 entity graph; the historical M1 agent is a stage-specific mechanism check, not a serialized upstream state provider

decision_rule: Authorize design of unprivileged V2-M4 only if every fixed gate passes on the one-shot fresh confirmation. Development results cannot authorize progression, and confirmation failure cannot be repaired by changing this protocol or rerunning its confirmation seeds.
